title: Minimum Moves to Reach Target in Grid
summary: Given points (sx, sy) and (tx, ty) on an infinite 2D grid, determine the least number of moves to reach (tx, ty) from (sx, sy).
statement: Given points (sx, sy) and (tx, ty) on an infinite 2D grid, determine the least number of moves to reach (tx, ty) from (sx, sy). At each step, you can move to (x + max(x, y), y) or (x, y + max(x, y)). If reaching (tx, ty) is impossible, return -1.
constraints: Coordinates are nonnegative and targets do not lie below the source.
A move adds max(x,y) to exactly one coordinate.
Return the minimum move count or -1 when unreachable.
hints: The larger target coordinate uniquely determines the previous state except when both coordinates are equal.
Reverse moves using subtraction below twice the other coordinate and halving above it.
At equality, try the two axis predecessors; memoize the branches.
These cases invert every possible forward move, while both coordinates decrease toward the source.
editorial: These cases invert every possible forward move, while both coordinates decrease toward the source.

tests.explanation: Increase y by two, then x by four, using two moves.
